units.rightText: Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the last farthing.
leftNotes: 5:26 literally, kodrantes. A kodrantes was a small copper coin worth about 2 lepta (widow’s mites)—not enough to buy very much of anything.

units.leftText: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery;’
units.rightText: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt not commit adultery:

units.leftText: but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.
units.rightText: but I say unto you, that every one that looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.

units.leftText: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
units.rightText: And if thy right eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body be cast into hell.

units.leftText: If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
units.rightText: And if thy right hand causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body go into hell.

units.leftText: “It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’
units.rightText: It was said also, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:

units.leftText: but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
units.rightText: but I say unto you, that every one that putteth away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, maketh her an adulteress: and whosoever shall marry her when she is put away committeth adultery.

units.leftText: “Again you have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’
units.rightText: Again, ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:

units.leftText: but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
units.rightText: but I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by the heaven, for it is the throne of God;

units.leftText: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
units.rightText: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

units.leftText: Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.
units.rightText: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, for thou canst not make one hair white or black.

units.leftText: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
units.rightText: But let your speech be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: and whatsoever is more than these is of the evil one.

units.leftText: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
units.rightText: Ye have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:

units.leftText: But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
units.rightText: but I say unto you, Resist not him that is evil: but whosoever smiteth thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

units.leftText: If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
units.rightText: And if any man would go to law with thee, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.

units.leftText: Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
units.rightText: And whosoever shall compel thee to go one mile, go with him two.

units.leftText: Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
units.rightText: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

units.leftText: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
units.rightText: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and hate thine enemy:
leftNotes: 5:43 not in the Bible, but see Qumran Manual of Discipline Ix, 21-26

units.leftText: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
units.rightText: but I say unto you, Love your enemies, and pray for them that persecute you;

units.leftText: that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
units.rightText: that ye may be sons of your Father who is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sendeth rain on the just and the unjust.

units.leftText: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
units.rightText: For if ye love them that love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?

units.leftText: If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
units.rightText: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the Gentiles the same?

units.leftText: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
units.rightText: Ye therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

units.leftText: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them: else ye have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.
leftNotes: 6:1 NU reads “acts of righteousness” instead of “charitable giving”

units.leftText: Therefore, when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
units.rightText: When therefore thou doest alms, sound not a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

units.leftText: But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
units.rightText: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

units.leftText: so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
units.rightText: that thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.

units.leftText: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
units.rightText: And when ye pray, ye shall not be as the hypocrites: for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

units.leftText: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
units.rightText: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thine inner chamber, and having shut thy door, pray to thy Father who is in secret, and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.

units.leftText: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
units.rightText: And in praying use not vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need before you ask him.
units.rightText: Be not therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

units.leftText: Pray like this:
units.rightText: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

units.leftText: Let your Kingdom come.
units.rightText: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.

units.leftText: Give us today our daily bread.
units.rightText: Give us this day our daily bread.

units.leftText: Forgive us our debts,
units.rightText: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

units.leftText: Bring us not into temptation,
units.rightText: And bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.

units.leftText: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
units.rightText: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

units.leftText: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
units.rightText: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

units.leftText: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
units.rightText: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen of men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

units.leftText: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
units.rightText: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thy head, and wash thy face;

units.leftText: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
units.rightText: that thou be not seen of men to fast, but of thy Father who is in secret: and thy Father, who seeth in secret, shall recompense thee.

units.leftText: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
units.rightText: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal:

units.leftText: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
units.rightText: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

units.leftText: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
units.rightText: for where thy treasure is, there will thy heart be also.

units.leftText: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
units.rightText: The lamp of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.

units.leftText: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
units.rightText: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is the darkness!

units.leftText: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
units.rightText: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
units.rightText: Therefore I say unto you, Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than the food, and the body than the raiment?

units.leftText: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
units.rightText: Behold the birds of the heaven, that they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; and your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are not ye of much more value than they?

units.leftText: “Which of you by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
units.rightText: And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit unto the measure of his life?

units.leftText: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
units.rightText: And why are ye anxious concerning raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

units.leftText: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
units.rightText: yet I say unto you, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

units.leftText: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
units.rightText: But if God doth so clothe the grass of the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

units.leftText: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
units.rightText: Be not therefore anxious, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

units.leftText: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
units.rightText: For after all these things do the Gentiles seek; for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

units.leftText: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
units.rightText: But seek ye first his kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
units.rightText: Be not therefore anxious for the morrow: for the morrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

units.leftText: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
units.rightText: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

units.leftText: For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
units.rightText: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured unto you.

units.leftText: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
units.rightText: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

units.leftText: Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
units.rightText: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me cast out the mote out of thine eye; and lo, the beam is in thine own eye?

units.leftText: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
units.rightText: Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.

units.leftText: “Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
units.rightText: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast your pearls before the swine, lest haply they trample them under their feet, and turn and rend you.

units.leftText: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
units.rightText: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

units.leftText: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
units.rightText: for every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

units.leftText: Or who is there among you who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
units.rightText: Or what man is there of you, who, if his son shall ask him for a loaf, will give him a stone;

units.leftText: Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
units.rightText: or if he shall ask for a fish, will give him a serpent?

units.leftText: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
units.rightText: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

units.leftText: Therefore, whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
units.rightText: All things therefore whatsoever ye would that men should do unto you, even so do ye also unto them: for this is the law and the prophets.

units.leftText: “Enter in by the narrow gate; for the gate is wide and the way is broad that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter in by it.
units.rightText: Enter ye in by the narrow gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many are they that enter in thereby.

units.leftText: How narrow is the gate and the way is restricted that leads to life! There are few who find it.
units.rightText: For narrow is the gate, and straitened the way, that leadeth unto life, and few are they that find it.

units.leftText: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
units.rightText: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.

units.leftText: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns or figs from thistles?
units.rightText: By their fruits ye shall know them. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

units.leftText: Even so, every good tree produces good fruit, but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
units.rightText: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but the corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

units.leftText: A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
units.rightText: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

units.leftText: Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
units.rightText: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

units.leftText: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
units.rightText: Therefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

units.leftText: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father who is in heaven.

units.leftText: Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
units.rightText: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy by thy name, and by thy name cast out demons, and by thy name do many mighty works?

units.leftText: Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
units.rightText: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

units.leftText: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.
units.rightText: Every one therefore that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them, shall be likened unto a wise man, who built his house upon the rock:

units.leftText: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
units.rightText: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon the rock.

units.leftText: Everyone who hears these words of mine and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
units.rightText: And every one that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand:

units.leftText: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it fell—and its fall was great.”
units.rightText: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and smote upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall thereof.

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching:

units.leftText: for he taught them with authority, and not like the scribes.
units.rightText: for he taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

units.leftText: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
units.rightText: And when he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

units.leftText: Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
units.rightText: And behold, there came to him a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

units.leftText: Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
units.rightText: And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway his leprosy was cleansed.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “See that you tell nobody; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

units.leftText: When he came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking him for help,
units.rightText: And when he was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,

units.leftText: saying, “Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”
units.rightText: and saying, Lord, my servant lieth in the house sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto him, I will come and heal him.

units.leftText: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
units.rightText: And the centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.

units.leftText: For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
units.rightText: For I also am a man under authority, having under myself soldiers: and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard it, he marveled and said to those who followed, “Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.
units.rightText: And when Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

units.leftText: I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,
units.rightText: And I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:

units.leftText: but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
units.rightText: but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast forth into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: Jesus said to the centurion, “Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.” His servant was healed in that hour.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And the servant was healed in that hour.

units.leftText: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.
units.rightText: And when Jesus was come into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick of a fever.

units.leftText: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. So she got up and served him.
units.rightText: And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she arose, and ministered unto him.

units.leftText: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons. He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick,
units.rightText: And when even was come, they brought unto him many possessed with demons: and he cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all that were sick:

units.leftText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.”
units.rightText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our diseases.

units.leftText: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes around him, he gave the order to depart to the other side.
units.rightText: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side.

units.leftText: A scribe came and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
units.rightText: And there came a scribe, and said unto him, Teacher, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

units.leftText: Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
units.rightText: And another of the disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

units.leftText: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”
units.rightText: But Jesus saith unto him, Follow me; and leave the dead to bury their own dead.

units.leftText: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
units.rightText: And when he was entered into a boat, his disciples followed him.

units.leftText: Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves; but he was asleep.
units.rightText: And behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the boat was covered with the waves: but he was asleep.

units.leftText: The disciples came to him and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We are dying!”
units.rightText: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Save, Lord; we perish.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

units.leftText: The men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
units.rightText: And the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?

units.leftText: When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes, two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.
units.rightText: And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gadarenes, there met him two possessed with demons, coming forth out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man could pass by that way.

units.leftText: Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”
units.rightText: And behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?

units.leftText: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.
units.rightText: Now there was afar off from them a herd of many swine feeding.

units.leftText: The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”

units.leftText: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers to receive his fruit.

units.rightText: But the husbandmen, when they saw the son, said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and take his inheritance.

units.rightText: And they took him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him.

units.leftText: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”

units.leftText: They told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruit in its season.”
units.rightText: They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will let out the vineyard unto other husbandmen, who shall render him the fruits in their seasons.

units.rightText: Again he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them that are bidden, Behold, I have made ready my dinner; my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come to the marriage feast.

units.leftText: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;
units.rightText: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;

units.leftText: and the rest grabbed his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them.

units.leftText: When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
units.rightText: But the king was wroth; and he sent his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.

units.rightText: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they that were bidden were not worthy.

units.rightText: Go ye therefore unto the partings of the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage feast.

units.rightText: And those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was filled with guests.

units.rightText: But when the king came in to behold the guests, he saw there a man who had not on a wedding-garment:

units.rightText: and he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding-garment? And he was speechless.

units.leftText: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.’
units.rightText: Then the king said to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and cast him out into the outer darkness; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: For many are called, but few chosen.”
units.rightText: For many are called, but few chosen.

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might entrap him in his talk.
units.rightText: Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might ensnare him in his talk.

units.leftText: They sent their disciples to him, along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and teach the way of God in truth, no matter whom you teach; for you aren’t partial to anyone.
units.rightText: And they send to him their disciples, with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and teachest the way of God in truth, and carest not for any one: for thou regardest not the person of men.

units.leftText: Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
units.rightText: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cæsar, or not?

units.leftText: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, “Why do you test me, you hypocrites?
units.rightText: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why make ye trial of me, ye hypocrites?

units.rightText: Show me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a denarius.

units.leftText: He asked them, “Whose is this image and inscription?”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?

units.leftText: They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
units.rightText: They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

units.leftText: When they heard it, they marveled, and left him and went away.
units.rightText: And when they heard it, they marvelled, and left him, and went away.

units.rightText: saying, Teacher, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

units.leftText: In the resurrection therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”
units.rightText: In the resurrection therefore whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
units.rightText: But Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.

units.leftText: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.
units.rightText: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as angels in heaven.

units.leftText: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,

units.leftText: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
units.rightText: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.

units.leftText: When the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.
units.rightText: And when the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.

units.rightText: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, gathered themselves together.

units.rightText: And one of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, trying him:

units.leftText: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the law?”
units.rightText: Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.

units.leftText: This is the first and great commandment.
units.rightText: This is the great and first commandment.

units.leftText: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
units.rightText: And a second like unto it is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.

units.leftText: The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”
units.rightText: On these two commandments the whole law hangeth, and the prophets.

units.leftText: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,
units.rightText: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,

units.leftText: saying, “What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?”
units.rightText: saying, What think ye of the Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The son of David.

units.leftText: He said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
units.rightText: He saith unto them, How then doth David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,

units.leftText: ‘The Lord said to my Lord,
units.rightText: The Lord said unto my Lord,

units.leftText: “If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
units.rightText: If David then calleth him Lord, how is he his son?

units.leftText: No one was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.
units.rightText: And no one was able to answer him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.

units.leftText: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes and to his disciples,
units.rightText: Then spake Jesus to the multitudes and to his disciples,

units.leftText: saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
units.rightText: saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat:

units.leftText: All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.
units.rightText: all things therefore whatsoever they bid you, these do and observe: but do not ye after their works; for they say, and do not.

units.leftText: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,

units.leftText: Neither be called masters, for one is your master, the Christ.
units.rightText: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your master, even the Christ.

units.leftText: But he who is greatest among you will be your servant.
units.rightText: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.
units.rightText: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye shut the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye enter not in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering in to enter.

units.rightText: Ye fools and blind: for which is greater, the gold, or the temple that hath sanctified the gold?

units.rightText: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gift that is upon it, he is a debtor.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye tithe mint and anise and cummin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law, justice, and mercy, and faith: but these ye ought to have done, and not to have left the other undone.

units.leftText: You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!
units.rightText: Ye blind guides, that strain out the gnat, and swallow the camel!

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and unrighteousness.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full from extortion and excess.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones and of all uncleanness.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.

units.leftText: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
units.rightText: Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but inwardly ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

units.rightText: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and garnish the tombs of the righteous,

units.leftText: Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,

units.rightText: that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous unto the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom ye slew between the sanctuary and the altar.

units.leftText: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!

units.leftText: Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way. His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
units.rightText: Then saith Jesus unto them, Fear not: go tell my brethren that they depart into Galilee, and there shall they see me.
leftNotes: 28:10 The word for “brothers” here may be also correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
units.rightText: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guard came into the city, and told unto the chief priests all the things that were come to pass.

units.leftText: When they were assembled with the elders and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
units.rightText: And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave much money unto the soldiers,

units.leftText: saying, “Say that his disciples came by night and stole him away while we slept.
units.rightText: saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.

units.leftText: If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
units.rightText: And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and rid you of care.

units.leftText: So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
units.rightText: So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continueth until this day.

units.leftText: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
units.rightText: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, unto the mountain where Jesus had appointed them.

units.leftText: When they saw him, they bowed down to him; but some doubted.
units.rightText: And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted.

units.leftText: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
units.rightText: And Jesus came to them and spake unto them, saying, All authority hath been given unto me in heaven and on earth.

units.leftText: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
units.rightText: Go ye therefore, and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit:

units.leftText: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
units.rightText: teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I commanded you: and lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world.
